subject: Reserve sizing control bands & GPU-price-linked discount request
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@brightlane.ai>, BrightLane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserve sizing control bands & GPU-price-linked discount request

Emily / BrightLane procurement team —

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, BrightLane is targeting a reserved/dedicated capacity commitment to support inference for their new summarization product. High level proposal we want to put on the table (attached):

- Initial committed pool: 150 A100-equivalent GPUs (equivalency matrix in pricing_model.xlsx)
- Term: 12 months, with phased activation (50% start month 1, +25% month 4, remainder month 7)
- Goal: predictable throughput for latency-sensitive flows and lower unit cost than on-demand

Two asks from the BrightLane side that we need internal clarity on before we send a formal SOW:
1) A GPU-price-linked discount structure: BrightLane wants a guaranteed % discount on our standard reserved rates, with the discount floored/adjusted if underlying GPU market costs spike. They asked for a 20% discount in our call.
2) Flex sizing / staging: confirmation we can legally and operationally stagger activation without full billing from day 1 (they want pro-rated provisioning).

Ben / Kim — can you review the attached model and confirm what discount band we can support under three scenarios (base, +20% GPU price shock, -10% GPU market tailwind)? We need recommended guardrails (e.g., up to 18% discount with auto-pass-through if GPU index > +15% etc.) so I can propose a single number to the customer. Also note procurement may ask about an escrow/credit if GPUs spike — include operational/finance flags if that requires exec approval.

Emily — we can share a draft SOW and activation schedule once we lock internal guardrails. Attached: pricing_model.xlsx and draft_sow.pdf. Expect an internal follow-up by EOB tomorrow.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), draft_sow.pdf (PDF)
From: Emily Jones <emily.jones@brightlane.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, BrightLane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve sizing control bands & GPU-price-linked discount request

Thanks Diego — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- Sizing: the 150 A100-equivalent target is our peak forecast; can we make the first tranche smaller (40%) and keep the same discount structure? Our ramp could be slower if we hit integration delays.
- Discount mechanics: we want a formula rather than a manual reprice. For example, discount = base_discount * (1 - max(0, GPU_index_change)/X). We realize we may need a cap.
- Escrow/credits: if you require an escrow, let us know the mechanics — we prefer a credit ladder rather than a cash escrow.

If you can provide three sensitivity rows (base / moderate spike / severe spike), we can review with finance and confirm whether a 12-month term is acceptable.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily
Emily Jones
Head of Procurement | BrightLane

--

Subject: Re: Reserve sizing control bands & GPU-price-linked discount request

Diego / Kim — attached is a compact sensitivity summary (sensitivity_summary.csv) with three scenarios and recommended discount guardrails. Summary below:

Scenario A — Base (expected GPU market)
- Underlying GPU cost index unchanged
- Committed pool: 150 A100-eq
- Recommended discount: 18% off standard reserved rate
- Billing: pro-rated by tranche as proposed

Scenario B — Moderate spike (+15% GPU index)
- Impact: supplier cost up ~12% (lagging index)
- Recommended discount: 12% (automatic auto-adjust down to this level if index > +10%)
- Mechanic: price-pass clause triggers; Redwood pays differential from credit ladder if spike persists > 60 days

Scenario C — Severe spike (+30% GPU index)
- Impact: supplier cost up ~25%
- Recommended discount: 6% (Redwood requests ability to re-negotiate or offer deferred ramp)
- Exec approval: any discount below 10% or any escrow over $250k requires VP-level finance approval

Operational notes:
- Staged activation OK — billing prorated to active capacity with clear activation dates in the SOW.
- Escrow vs credit ladder: recommend credit ladder tied to usage thresholds (we avoid holding cash escrow where possible).

I attached the CSV with the math and simple cost-to-Redwood delta. If we want to be competitive but protected, I recommend we offer 18% in our first outbound with an automatic floor of 12% at +10% GPU index and an explicit exec re-eval at +25%. That maps to our internal approval ladder.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Deal Structuring | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sensitivity_summary.csv (CSV)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Jones <emily.jones@brightlane.ai>, BrightLane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve sizing control bands & GPU-price-linked discount request

Thanks Ben — this is clear and a good starting point. A few governance points for Diego to present to BrightLane:

1) Approval ladder (internal):
   - Manager (Ben) signoff: discounts up to 18% and escrow/credit up to $150k
   - Director signoff: discounts >18% up to 25% and escrow/credit between $150k–$250k
   - VP/CFO signoff: discounts >25% or escrow > $250k or any contract language that materially alters our indemnities

2) Contract mechanics: we must include a clear GPU-index definition, data source (public market index URL), a 30–60 day lookback window for triggering adjustments, and an arbitration clause for index disputes.

3) Suggested customer-facing framing: offer 18% firm with an indexed floor (12%) if the GPU index moves > +10%. If BrightLane wants a 20% firm discount, we can propose a 20% conditional discount that steps down to 12% on trigger and requires a credit ladder equal to 3 months' committed spend.

Diego — if you are comfortable, propose the 18% firm / 12% floor with documented pass-through mechanics and the staging plan. Ask BrightLane if they want the conditional 20% (with credit ladder) as an alternative. I will sign off at manager level; anything above that I will escalate.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Pricing | Redwood Inference

--

Emily — appreciate the patience while we ran this up the chain. Quick summary / proposal from Redwood:

- Offer A (standard): 18% firm discount on reserved rates, 12-month term, staged activation (40% / 30% / 30%), billing pro-rated to active capacity.
- Offer B (conditional): 20% discount with a credit ladder equal to 3 months' committed spend; automatic step-down to 12% if GPU index > +10% for >45 days.
- Price-pass mechanics: use published GPU index (link in SOW), 30-day lookback for trigger, Redwood and BrightLane can request arbitration within 7 business days of a trigger event.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether BrightLane prefers Offer A or Offer B (if B, we will need the credit ladder schedule).
2) If you accept A, we'll send a revised SOW and DocuSign link for signature.

Link to revised proposal and signature: https://app.docusign.com/BRL-0423/exec-sign

I'll attach a clean one-pager and the updated SOW to the DocuSign envelope. If you want the conditional 20% we will route for director approval (Kim) and possibly VP signoff depending on the credit ladder size.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the mechanics before committing.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
